title: Non-Interrupting Stop Predicate for In-Progress Gate Conversations
summary: The active cycle entry gains a `**In-progress gate:**` field (e.g., `decide → architect`) that the orchestrator sets at the start of an AID phase-boundary gate and clears when the gate-reflection note is written. While the field is set, the Stop hook returns allow without running the gate-reflection-note check for that named boundary, while other manifest checks for the source phase, and the compound check (ADR-064) for any dispatch that fires, continue to run. If the orchestrator fails to set the field the hook reverts to its existing blocking behavior (safe failure); if it fails to clear the field the note check is silently skipped, mitigated by a per-session advisory notice and a `/rdd-conform` heuristic.
workflow_point: phase-boundary AID gate conversations; cycle-status.md top entry
mechanism: In-progress gate field plus Stop hook non-interrupting predicate that skips only the gate-reflection-note check

links.note: extends ADR-063's per-phase manifest format with an optional artifact_type: aid-cycle-gate-reflection field so the hook can selectively skip only the gate-reflection-note entry when In-progress gate is set

the compound check (ADR-064) and revision-aware re-audit reminder continue to fire for non-gate dispatches during an in-progress gate; the in-progress-gate predicate relaxes only the gate's own artifact requirement
the In-progress gate field declares that the gate-reflection note (ADR-066) is being produced during the gate; the note's appearance signals the gate's completion and clears the field

uses the same structural pattern as ADR-072 (a per-entry field the hook reads before dispatching to the manifest check); the unsafe failure mode here is the analog of ADR-072's Fails-Safe-to-Allow risk applied to this field
the In-progress gate field lives per cycle entry within ADR-078's multi-cycle stack schema
